newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-LUYT BACKS INTERNATIONAL RETURN FOR SMALL.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-LUYT BACKS INTERNATIONAL RETURN FOR SMALL.

text.p: South African Rugby Football Union (SARFU) president Louis Luyt intervened on Wednesday to help smooth the return of out-of-favour Natal wing James Small to the Springbok team.
Small, the most capped Springbok in the post-isolation period with 31 appearances, has not played for South Africa since a Tri-Nations match against New Zealand in Cape Town on August 10.
The 27-year-old wing was subsequently dropped for disciplinary reasons after he was spotted in a nightclub in the early hours of the morning two days before that Newlands test.
A SARFU management committee, represented by Luyt and SARFU junior vice-president Johan Claassen, met Small in Johannesburg on Wednesday morning to open the way for the player's return.
A SARFU statement said Small had been reminded by the committee of the "format of South African rugby and what is expected of a professional player of his calibre".

Luyt said in the statement: "The management committee facilitated this meeting to end the speculation over James and we feel positive steps have now been taken to clear any obstacles that prevent his eligibility for selection in the Springbok team.
"James is a world-class player and an asset to any side but a change in attitude was needed before he could best serve South African rugby."
Luyt has made a recommendation to national coach Andre Markgraaff that Small should become available for selection.
The South African squad to tour Argentina, France and Wales in November and December is to be announced in Durban on October 12.
